title: Release feedback loop and hotfix paths for private deployments
content:
Purpose:
This working doc outlines a compact, pragmatic feedback loop and hotfix paths for private deployments (VPC / on-prem) with emphasis on: reproducible Terraform module upgrades, deterministic Helm value layering, GitOps-driven ArgoCD promotion flows, and image signing/attestation for airgapped customers. It focuses on the release mechanics operators and SREs will run during upgrades and emergency patches.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to private deployments managed via ArgoCD-based GitOps with Helm charts packaged in internal OCI registry (airgap-friendly).
- Terraform modules are used to provision infra (VPC, bastions, ECR/OCI proxy, k8s clusters).
- Image signing is done with cosign; we maintain signed manifests and a local attestation cache for airgap.
- Customers may be online or airgapped; playbook includes steps for both.

Key principles:
1) Immutable artifact bundles: every release is a single SHA-bundled manifest (helm chart tgz sha + image digest list + terraform module tag).
2) Preflight gating: automated gates run in ephemeral test tenant as close as possible to customer environment (same k8s version, same ingress).
3) Fast rollback: every promotion must register a rollback commit and a tested rollback pipeline.
4) Minimal blast radius: canaries use traffic mirroring and tenant-scoped rollouts (ephemeral tenant for validation).

High-level release flow (happy path):
- Step 0: Build & Sign
  - Build container images in CI. Tag with semantic build id (e.g. 20250203.1). Push to staging registry.
  - cosign sign --key ksm://projects/… <image>@sha256:<digest> and upload attestation to SLSA provenance bucket.
  - Package helm chart (Chart.yaml version bumped). Compute chart tgz sha. Create artifact-bundle.json with chart_sha, image digests, terraform_module_tag.

- Step 1: Terraform module staging
  - Use versioned terraform module (module_tag). Run a dry-run plan against a staging VPC replica. Store plan and plan signature as artifacts.
  - Validate state migration scripts (if any) in a disposable cluster.

- Step 2: ArgoCD canary promotion (App-of-Apps pattern)
  - Push desired app manifests into the canary repo path: apps/customer-x/canary/{{bundle_sha}}.
  - ArgoCD syncs into canary cluster namespace. Run smoke job (see tests below).
  - Mirror production-like traffic to canary (service-mesh HTTP mirroring or ingress-level duplicate-post). Monitor error rates and latency (SLO thresholds).
  - If canary stable for N minutes (configurable), promote to partial production (10–25% nodes) by updating k8s selector via ArgoCD patch.

- Step 3: Full promotion
  - After staged metrics pass, update apps/customer-x/prod/{{bundle_sha}}. ArgoCD sync performs rollout. Finalize by recording deployment manifest and a signed promotion tag in Git.

- Step 4: Post-deploy verification & automated rollback hook
  - Automated post-checks (end-to-end smoke, dependency health checks, KV cache warmup). Any failure triggers ArgoCD rollback using the recorded rollback commit. Documented SLA: 15-minute detection + automated rollback if critical.

Hotfix and emergency patch path:
- Trigger: high-severity customer outage or security CVE detected in runtime image.
- Quick patch branch flow:
  1. Create hotfix/<customer>-<shortid> branch from prod manifest commit.
  2. Replace only affected image tags (use pre-signed image digests if available).
  3. Minimal terraform changes only if absolutely required (avoid infra drift during emergency).
  4. Run CI high-priority smoke test suite (fast subset).
  5. If passes, PR to prod with required approvals; merge triggers ArgoCD fast-track sync with enforced sync-waves (canary, then quick prod if canary OK).
  6. Record incident ticket and attach signed artifact bundle.

Airgap-specific considerations:
- Artifact bundle export: create oci-bundle.tar that includes chart tgz, image tarballs, cosign signatures, and terraform module tgz. Operator runs artifact import to internal OCI proxy which validates signatures against cached public keys.
- Signature staleness: maintain a local 'signature cache' TTL and an offline pubkey store. Documented manual steps for key rotation and offline verification.

Preflight & smoke tests (example list):
- k8s readiness and liveness probes for core pods
- sample end-to-end request through ingress with status 200 and body checks
- KV cache warmup within 60s and response latency under 50ms P95 for small payloads
- Model server warm start (kv cache hit on repeated prompt)
- Basic auth/KMS integration smoke if customer uses KMS provider
- DB migration dry-run check: migration plan applies cleanly and is reversible

Terraform module upgrade notes (operational checklist):
- Pin module versions in customer root module. Do not rely on floating tags.
- Keep a migration_scripts/ directory adjacent to module with explicit step-by-step migration commands and 'undo' tasks.
- Use terraform plan -out and cosign sign the plan file for auditability. Store signed plan in artifact storage.

Helm value layering and deterministic overrides:
- Base chart: vendor-maintained core values.
- customer-values.yaml: customer specific overrides, checked into customer repo path but encrypted at rest if necessary.
- environment overlays: canary.yaml, prod.yaml applied by ArgoCD kustomize layering.
- Implement a validation job that computes final values (helm template --values merged) and checks for unexpected feature flags.

Attestation and provenance:
- Each promotion must publish a signed provenance record with fields: bundle_sha, image_digests[], terraform_module_tag, geo-region, promoter, timestamp, signatures[]. Keep copies in per-customer artifact store and central audit bucket.

Rollback decision matrix (quick reference):
- Severity P0 (customer down): immediate rollback to last-good-bundle, notify customer success and incident commander.
- Severity P1 (degraded): hold canary, run targeted debug tests; if unresolved in 30 minutes escalate to rollback.
- Severity P2/P3: queued for next maintenance window with full postmortem.

Operational runbook snippets (commands and quick references):
- Generate artifact bundle: ./scripts/make-bundle.sh --chart ./charts/core --images images.list --out bundle-20250203.tar
- Sign bundle manifest: cosign sign-blob --key ksm://… bundle-manifest.json
- ArgoCD promote: git commit -m "promote: {{bundle_sha}}" && git push origin prod && argocd app sync customer-x-prod --async
- Force rollback: argocd app rollback customer-x-prod 1 --prune

Monitoring and post-release telemetry:
- Ensure per-route token-level latency and token-cost metrics are reported to Console for the promoted bundle. Tag metrics with bundle_sha for quick attribution.
- Automated regression detection: compare recent production bundle to last-good using eval prompt set A/B test harness; auto-alert on semantic drift beyond threshold.

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Define exact TTL and refresh pattern for airgap signature cache and pubkey rotation cadence.
- Decide on automated DB migration ban during canary vs. allow on canary but block for full promotion.
- Integrate SLSA provenance publication into the main CI pipeline (currently a manual step in some repos).

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call to enact emergency rollback:
1) Identify last-good-bundle from artifact registry.
2) Create rollback git commit referencing last-good-bundle and push to prod branch.
3) Trigger argocd app sync and monitor pods.
4) If terraform infra change needed to support rollback, run terraform apply using the signed plan (operator approval required).
5) Notify CS + customer and create incident timeline entry.

Notes: This doc is intentionally procedural and minimal; next steps are to translate into a runnable automation repo (scripts + github actions + argocd app-of-apps templates) and a one-click operator dashboard for emergency rollbacks.
